content: This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as those measuring sex hormone-binding globulin or thyroid function, potentially leading to inaccurate results. If someone overdoses and experiences severe symptoms like loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call emergency services (911) immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. In the U.S., you can call 1-800-222-1222, and in Canada, call 1-844-764-7669. Follow your doctor’s instructions for self-examining your breasts and report any lumps immediately. If you miss a dose, refer to the product’s package information for specific guidance. You may need to use additional birth control methods, such as condoms or spermicides, to prevent pregnancy. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into drains unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. It is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Common side effects of this medication may include nausea, vomiting, headache, bloating, breast tenderness, or weight gain. Vaginal bleeding between periods (spotting) or missed/irregular periods may also occur. If these effects persist or worsen, inform your doctor or pharmacist promptly. Remember, this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits outweigh the risks of side effects. Serious allergic reactions to this drug are rare. For any concerns about side effects, contact your doctor. Before using this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to norethindrone, other progestins, or any other substances. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. Limit your time in the sun, avoid tanning booths and sunlamps, and use sunscreen or protective clothing when outdoors. This medication should not be used during pregnancy and may pass into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription, non-prescription, and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Some drugs, such as griseofulvin, modafinil, rifamycins (e.g., rifampin, rifabutin), ritonavir, and St. John’s Wort, may reduce the effectiveness of hormonal birth control by decreasing hormone levels in your body, potentially leading to pregnancy. Discuss with your doctor whether you should use additional reliable birth control methods. This medication may interfere with certain lab tests, such as those for sex hormone-binding globulin or thyroid function, potentially causing false results. Always inform your healthcare provider and laboratory personnel that you are using this medication. For overdose situations, if someone has severe symptoms like passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Avoid flushing medications down the toilet or pouring them into drains unless instructed. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Always consult your healthcare provider for the most accurate and personalized advice regarding this medication.
